title: Traffic Telescope — Readiness Notebook & Burn/Triage Playbook
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, fast-moving notebook for the upcoming go-live window. Think: a telescope (longer view) + a triage flashlight (spotlights immediate fixes). Goal is to capture signals, ownerable actions, and quick decision heuristics to keep latency and cost within target while we ramp traffic.

Audience: product-ops, release eng, SRE, serving-runtime, solutions-engineering.

Context + constraints:
- Feature: chat-completions + streaming, model v3.2 pinned for hosted and Dedicated fallback to v3-quant when under pressure.
- Launch target: progressive beta to 10k DAU then step to 100k over 2 weeks.
- SLAs: p50 <= 220ms, p95 <= 650ms for small (<=128 tokens) requests; cost budget baseline: incremental token cost <= $0.0009/token.
- Known risk: KV cache cold-start on new users, autoscaler warm-up ~45s on dedicated pools, and prefix cache TTL default 6hrs is too low for repeat prompts.

Key signals to watch (Traffic Telescope):
- Traffic & ramp metrics: requests/min, new sessions/min, peak concurrent streams.
- Latency buckets: p50/p90/p95/p99 (segmented by model, deployment type, and sequence length).
- Error surface: 5xx rate, timeouts, model OOMs, token stream stalls.
- Cost telemetry: tokens generated, tokens billed (quantized vs fp), per-request cost estimate.
- Cache health: KV cache hit rate, prefix-cache eviction rate, median KV lookup latency.
- Autoscaler: pool fill%, queue length, scale-up event duration, warm-up failures.
- Fallback occurrences: number of requests routed to lower-cost variants and success/latency delta.

Primary KPIs to keep green (tracked on sprintboard):
- User-facing: p95 latency (overall), successful-stream-rate, error-rate (<0.5% target).
- Operational: median scale-up time (<60s), KV cache hit rate (>65% after 6h ramp), fallback rate (<5% sustained).
- Cost: rolling 24h cost delta compared to baseline (<+15%).

Readiness checklist (pre-roll / T minus):
- Pre-roll (~72h):
  - Confirm model artifact pinned and digest verified (owner: applied-ml).
  - Run load sims using representative prompt set (owner: serving-runtime). 3 runs at 1x/3x/10x expected beta.
  - Validate autoscaler policy in staging with synthetic traffic that mimics 95th percentile burst (owner: platform-engineering).
  - Increase prefix-cache TTL to 24h for beta cohort (owner: infra / feature flag).
  - Confirm rollback routing exists: immediate route to stable-v2 with gradual traffic drain (owner: product-ops).
  - On-call rotation confirmed and paging thresholds set in Ops channel (owner: SRE).

- Pre-roll (~24h):
  - Smoke test streaming on all client SDKs and verify chunk reassembly (owner: developer-experience).
  - Confirm CORS, rate limits, and quota enforcement rules for early adopters (owner: api-platform).
  - Sanity-check billing pipeline (tokens -> cost) for sample traffic (owner: finance-ops).
  - Stakeholder readout with GTM and CS (owner: product-ops).

Fast triage cookbook (live during ramp):
- If p95 jumps > 150% above baseline for 5m:
  1) Check cost vs fallback ratio. If fallback rate > 10% AND p95 higher on fallback, route traffic back to pinned variant (action owner: product-ops + infra).
  2) Inspect autoscaler queues: long queue length -> temporarily enable burst capacity pool (owner: platform-engineering).
  3) If memory errors on hosts: reduce max_concurrency on pool and enable backpressure (owner: serving-runtime).

- If KV cache hit rate < 40% after 2h of ramp:
  1) Increase prefix-cache TTL or force prewarm of top 200 prefixes (owner: solutions-engineering).
  2) Re-route high-frequency prompts to cached-only path where we serve with strong prefix-match heuristic (owner: serving-runtime + product-ops).

- If cost per token > baseline by 25% sustained over 6h:
  1) Throttle non-essential batch jobs (owner: infra).
  2) Activate model quantization fallback for non-latency-critical routes (owner: applied-ml).
  3) Notify finance and create short-term cost cap with spike policy (owner: finance-ops + SRE).

Decision heuristics (yes/no shortcuts):
- Rollback to previous stable version if: error-rate > 1% OR p95 > 2x baseline for > 30m without clear mitigation.
- Pause beta ramp if: autoscaler warm-up time > 2x expected OR queue length > threshold for > 1h.
- Continue ramp if: p95 within +25% of baseline and KV hit-rate approaching target with active mitigations.

Owner matrix (quick):
- Owner: applied-ml -> model digest + quantization plan + safety regressions.
- Owner: serving-runtime -> streaming stability, concurrency toggles, memory safety.
- Owner: platform-engineering -> autoscaler scripts, burst pool toggles, infra provisioning.
- Owner: product-ops -> traffic decisions, stakeholder comms, canary sizing.
- Owner: SRE -> oncall escalation, pager thresholds, postmortem if needed.

Rolling playbook snippets (copy/paste into Ops channel):
- \"ALERT: p95 (last 5m) x% over baseline, queue len y, KV hit z%. Product-ops recommends: [option1] route x% to stable-v2, [option2] enable burst pool. Owners: platform-eng, serving-runtime.\"

Quick probes to run (owner + cmd):
- Top-100 prefixes prewarm (solutions-eng): curl -X POST /prewarm -d '{prefix_list:[...]}' (use staging key)
- Simulate 3x burst with streaming toggles off (serving-runtime): run ./loadgen --burst=3 --streaming=false --seq=64
- Cost sanity: sample-bill.sh --window 60m (finance-ops)

Unresolved questions / risks to call out:
- Can we temporarily increase dedicated burst pool beyond committed capacity without long lead? (platform-engineering conversation with sales needed)
- Are there any overlooked quota rules in EU region that may cause silent 429s for EU early adopters?
- How will function-calling feature interact with KV cache when callers issue many short-lived tools?

Post-launch capture (first 72h):
- Quick postmortem template to fill in within 6h of any high-severity signal: what happened, root cause hypothesis, immediate mitigation, long-term fix, TL;DR for execs. (owner: oncall SRE + product-ops)
- Collect prompt-level examples for any quality regressions and attach to eval suite (owner: applied-ml + product-ops).
- Run cost reconciliation against baseline and classify excess spend by cause (owner: finance-ops).

Notes to self (scattered):
- Keep the telescope pointed at long-term signals: user engagement vs latency tradeoff; if we see engagement drop correlated with >200ms p95 increase, consider temporary exposure cap per user.
- Remember to de-escalate: many transient spikes resolve after a single scale-up; only escalate if persistent or error-related.

Appendix: short checklist to paste into ticket description:
- [ ] pinned model digest verified
- [ ] 3 load sims complete and artifacts uploaded
- [ ] autoscaler policy validated in staging
- [ ] prefix-cache TTL updated for beta cohort
- [ ] burst pool toggle tested
- [ ] oncall rotation confirmed and pager thresholds set
- [ ] smoke test SDK streaming OK

If you’re reading this and have a mitigation idea that isn’t listed: add a short note below with your name and we’ll triage at the next 15m check-in.

-- Claire H.
traffic telescope owner (product-ops)
